subject: Agriculture
title: Rural Inequality
description: Learn Rural Inequality in one minute.

hook.text: The Green Revolution boosted production—but the benefits weren't shared equally.

buildup.text: Farmers with land, water, and capital adopted quickly. Landless laborers and tiny plot holders could not.

discovery.text: Wealthier farmers bought neighbors' land. Farm sizes grew at the top while small holders were squeezed out.

twist.text: In many regions, the gap between rich and poor farmers widened during the yield boom, not narrowed.

climax.text: Rural migration to cities accelerated as small-scale farming became uncompetitive.

punchline.text: More food for everyone. More wealth for some.

quiz.question: How did the Green Revolution affect rural inequality?
options: It often widened the gap between wealthy farmers and landless laborers
It had no effect on inequality

details.summary: The Green Revolution increased total food production but unevenly distributed its benefits, often widening the gap between wealthy and poor farmers. Those with land, irrigation, and credit adopted first and profited most, while landless laborers and marginal farmers were frequently displaced.
details.whyItMatters: Rural inequality is the Green Revolution's most debated legacy. Understanding how technology adoption creates winners and losers is essential for designing agricultural policies that improve food production without deepening social divides.
takeaways: Green Revolution benefits concentrated among farmers with land, water, and credit access
Landless laborers and tenant farmers were frequently displaced by mechanization
Regional disparities emerged between irrigated areas that prospered and rain-fed areas left behind

faq.question: How did the Green Revolution increase rural inequality?
faq.answer: Wealthier farmers adopted high-yield technology first, earned more, bought more land, and mechanized—displacing hired laborers. Small farmers without irrigation or credit couldn't compete and many sold their land.

faq.question: Were there efforts to make Green Revolution technologies more equitable?
faq.answer: Land reform programs, cooperative credit systems, and subsidized inputs aimed to broaden access but had mixed success. India's public distribution system channeled cheap grain to the poor.
